key_insight: MDSKILL proposes multi-view distillation to help agents internalize reusable skills from textual memories rather than rely only on skill prompts. It targets the noisy, overlapping, and conflicting knowledge that makes direct self-distillation difficult.
problem_solved: Self-generated skill memories can improve agent learning, but their noise and entangled knowledge make them difficult to distill efficiently into a policy under limited training budgets.
method: Use textual skill memories to guide agent trajectories and complement reinforcement learning.
Apply on-policy self-distillation to provide dense, fine-grained supervision from skill-guided trajectories.
Introduce multi-view distillation to support skill internalization; the supplied abstract is truncated, so its specific mechanisms are unavailable.
impact: The approach could make experience-driven agent improvement more training-efficient by transferring useful skills into the policy itself. Quantitative gains cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Pipeline: past experiences → textual skill memory → guided trajectories → distillation → updated policy.
Memory cards illustrating noisy, redundant, and conflicting instructions.

Before-and-after illustration contrasting external skill prompts with internalized policy skills.
paper_title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
paper_authors: Dian Jin, Jinluan Yang, Kairong Han, Baohong Li, Zijing Hu
